idea.title: The Lake That Killed Without a Sound
idea.premise: In 1986, Lake Nyos released an invisible carbon-dioxide cloud that moved into nearby villages while the water still looked calm.
idea.audience_promise: Follow the hidden chain from volcanic gas beneath the lake to the silent disaster and the engineering response.
idea.central_question: How did a calm volcanic lake kill more than seventeen hundred people overnight?

truth.disclosure: This episode recounts the verified Lake Nyos gas disaster; stock footage is used as clearly representational visual coverage.

causal_chain.cause: Volcanic activity fed carbon dioxide into the deep water of Lake Nyos.
escalation: The gas accumulated invisibly for years.
A rare limnic eruption released it into the valley.
The heavier-than-air cloud displaced breathable oxygen in nearby villages.
causal_chain.consequence: More than seventeen hundred people and thousands of animals died overnight.
causal_chain.why_it_mattered: The disaster led to degassing pipes and monitoring of other volcanic lakes.

promise_payoff.promise: A lake that looks peaceful can conceal a lethal mechanism.
promise_payoff.payoff: The final lesson connects Lake Nyos to ongoing monitoring and engineered degassing.

visual_feasibility.note: Twelve unique clips passed sampled-frame QA with dedicated industrial piping and valve inserts. Stock footage remains explicitly representational; final approval is waiting on narration and captions.

editorial.notes: Story, visual route and factual framing passed editorial red-team. Audio alignment remains a separate technical gate.

factual.notes: Core claims are sourced to NASA, USGS and peer-reviewed literature.

monetization.notes: No graphic imagery or harmful instructions.

sources.title: Lake Nyos, Cameroon
facts: Carbon dioxide from Lake Nyos moved into the valley and killed nearly 1,800 people and 3,500 livestock.

sources.title: The 21 August 1986 Lake Nyos Gas Disaster in Cameroon
facts: The USGS report documents the volcanic setting and carbon-dioxide release mechanism.

sources.title: The 1986 Lake Nyos gas disaster in Cameroon, West Africa
facts: Peer-reviewed evidence supports carbon dioxide stored in deep lake water as the source.

uncertainties: The exact trigger of the limnic eruption remains debated in the literature.
